newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks close down, earlier gains lost.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks close down, earlier gains lost.

text.p: Seoul stocks closed slightly lower on Thursday as late profit-taking on recent risers wiped out earlier gains, brokers said.
They said the market may attempt a rebound on Friday, but it would be short-lived.
The composite stock index closed down 0.65 points to 744.34. Losers outpaced gainers 417 to 373, with 44.38 million shares changing hands.
Brokers said selling in the afternoon focused on individual issues that have risen in the past couple of days.

Brokers said an improved economic forecast from a business group helped the rise. The Federation of Korean Industries revised upwards its forecast for this year's gross domestic product growth to 5.9 percent from 5.5 percent.
Samsung Electronics rose 500 won to 70,000, and SK Telecom added 8,000 won to 450,000.

Brokers said petrochemical shares rose on expectations of benefits following a chemical plant explosion at Shell Oil near Houston, the United States, on Sunday. Local papers carried the news this morning.
Honam Petrochemical rose 900 won to its daily limit high of 13,000, and Hanwha Chemical gained 340 won to 7,290.
Brokers said bargain hunting on the securities sector reversed losses in early morning. The securities sub-index rose 4.28 percent to 1,318.52 points.

Chohung Bank was the most actively traded stock with 3.4 million shares changing hands. An additional 4.39 percent of the bank's outstanding common shares become newly available for foreign investment from Thursday.
